answer: A velvet rope that costs real capital to pass: every identity must escrow stake to enter the harbor, held through many epochs of honest work before reputation unlocks any weight. The ledger is a glacier — append-only, replayable by anyone — so each alias's history and timing patterns are permanently checkable, and collusion clusters betray themselves on that record. Slash the stake on proven collusion and the economics invert: an attacker funds one locked deposit per fake identity, and every bust freezes that capital. Mass aliases stop being cheap — they become a slow, expensive, public grind.
